clue.text: Hood, good Sarkozy-style, to cover bag

blocks.note: bon is French for good, and Sarkozy was a French president
to bag a catch is to net it

explanation.surface: A French-style hood is pulled over a bag, as if disguising a robber.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer the first piece sits on top of the second, so 'to cover' places the French word above the catch-word.
explanation.definitionFit: A bonnet is a soft head covering tied under the chin, a kind of hood; in Britain it is also a car's engine cover.

clue.text: Tactless girl's puncturing sad, loveless erection

indicators.note: love is zero in tennis scoring, so being without love means dropping that round letter
something in a sad state is a wreck, so the remaining letters are jumbled
to puncture something is to go into it, so one piece is pushed inside the other

blocks.note: Di is a girl's name, plus the S of the possessive
taken as written before losing its love letter

explanation.surface: A girl's tactless remark deflates a man's unhappy, unloving erection.
explanation.walkthrough: Love is O, from the zero in tennis scores; Di is the stock short form of Diana.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone indiscreet lacks prudence in what they say, which is a close synonym of tactless.

clue.text: see 4dn.
(& 3dn.) Numb butts not welcomed by go-ahead types

definitions.note: a description of the thing rather than a synonym

blocks.note: a numb limb is said to have gone dead
butts are the ends of cigarettes

explanation.surface: Numb backsides are not wanted by energetic go-getters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Butts' tempts a reading as bottoms, which fits the surface, but here it means cigarette stubs.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambitious, go-ahead people dislike blind alleys and situations with no prospect of progress, which is what dead ends are.

clue.text: Evil controller, Sun, leaving in disgrace

indicators.note: something in disgrace has fallen out of its proper order, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: S is the standard abbreviation for Sun or Sunday
the letters of this word, rearranged

explanation.surface: A wicked boss at the Sun newspaper quits in disgrace.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sun is a British tabloid, which makes the surface read like a newspaper scandal.
explanation.definitionFit: Svengali is the sinister hypnotist in du Maurier's novel Trilby, whose name now means anyone who manipulates others.

clue.text: State of our old PM releasing grip of celebrated car crash victim

indicators.note: the grip is the two hands at either end, so letting go removes the outside letters

blocks.note: Benjamin Disraeli was a British Prime Minister in the 1800s
Princess Diana, popularly Di, died in a Paris car crash in 1997

explanation.surface: A dark scene: a former prime minister lets go of a famous car crash victim.
explanation.walkthrough: The outer letters of DISRAELI are D and I, which spell DI; dropping them leaves ISRAEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Israel is a sovereign country in the Middle East, and a state is a political nation.

clue.text: Poet 'doing a Gordon'?

blocks.note: first meaning: Robert or Elizabeth Barrett ..., Victorian poets
second meaning: behaving like Gordon Brown, UK Prime Minister 2007-10

explanation.walkthrough: The second meaning is a playful coinage: to act like Gordon Brown is to be 'Brown-ing'.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Browning wrote dramatic monologues; the surname also reads as a made-up verb from the politician's surname.

clue.text: Brown got by balls – name the joker!

blocks.note: buff is a pale yellowish-brown colour
two balls look like two round O letters
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: Gordon Brown is mocked as a buffoon who has been bested by Ed Balls.
explanation.walkthrough: Brown and Balls look like the politicians Gordon Brown and Ed Balls, but Brown is a colour and balls are round letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A buffoon is a clown who plays the fool, so 'joker' is a close synonym.

clue.text: Penny and rock star moved when having a shag

definitions.note: a description of the body part rather than a synonym

blocks.note: P is the abbreviation for penny
Elvis Presley, the King of Rock and Roll

explanation.surface: A cheap fling with a rock star who swivels his hips.
explanation.walkthrough: Shag is British slang for sex. Elvis was nicknamed 'Elvis the Pelvis' for his hip-swinging, which makes the clue apt.
explanation.definitionFit: The pelvis is the hip bone structure, which thrusts during intercourse.

clue.text: Horrible turd comes round to admit Cameron's final decline

indicators.note: something horrible is a mess, so the word that follows is jumbled
to come round something is to surround it, so one piece goes inside the other
the final of a name means only its last letter is used

blocks.note: the letters of this word, rearranged
to own up is to admit
the last letter of the former Prime Minister's name

explanation.surface: A political mess forces David Cameron to concede a slump.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged turd wraps around OWN after its first letter, and Cameron's last letter finishes it.
explanation.definitionFit: A downturn is a fall in economic activity, so a decline in fortunes.

clue.text: Staleness round middle of penis? Stick iodine on growth

indicators.note: the middle of a five-letter word is its third letter only
going round something means surrounding it, so one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: a fug is a stale, stuffy atmosphere
the central letter of this five-letter word
I is the chemical symbol for iodine

explanation.surface: A medical worry: a stale smell around the penis, treated by dabbing iodine on a growth.
explanation.walkthrough: FUG goes round N, and I is added at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Fungi are organisms such as mushrooms and moulds, and a fungal infection is a growth on the body.

clue.text: Quite peaky, this pissed Adonis comes round promptly

definitions.note: a description of the region rather than a synonym

indicators.note: pissed is British slang for drunk, and drunk letters stagger out of order
coming round something surrounds it, so one piece is placed within the other

blocks.note: the letters of this name, rearranged
to do something promptly is to do it now

explanation.surface: A drunk handsome youth looks rather ill but soon recovers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peaky' wants to mean pale and sickly, which fits the drunk in the surface; here it means full of peaks.
explanation.definitionFit: Snowdonia is the mountainous national park in north Wales around Snowdon, so it is a peak-filled area.

clue.text: Eye's description when drunken sot bows out of post-coital confusion?

indicators.note: one who bows out leaves, so these letters are taken away from the longer word
a drunk staggers, so the letters to remove are scattered rather than in a row
confusion means disorder, so the letters left are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written; a sot is a drunkard
taken as written

explanation.surface: A drunk staggers away from a muddled bedroom scene after sex.
explanation.walkthrough: The S, O and T come out of POSTCOITAL at scattered places, leaving PCOITAL to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Optical means relating to sight, so it is the adjective you would use to describe the eye.

clue.text: Clear expression of woman stifling Cyclops on date with sex

indicators.note: to stifle something is to smother it, so the other pieces are wrapped inside

blocks.note: Lucy is a woman's name
the setter Cyclops refers to themselves as I
D is the abbreviation for date
it is a coy word for sex

explanation.surface: A woman smothers the setter on a date involving sex.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'on' places I above D; LUCY then wraps round IDIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucidity is clarity of thought or language, so it is the quality of clear expression.

clue.text: Nothing vulgar about groupie having tumble

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the word that follows faces the other way

blocks.note: a groupie is an obsessive fan
a tumble is a fall

explanation.surface: There is nothing coarse about a groupie who trips over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vulgar' looks like wordplay for naff (tacky), but it belongs to the definition: a slang phrase for nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Naff all is British slang meaning absolutely nothing, a mild euphemism for a ruder phrase.

clue.text: Act odd with a coffee? That's not how the bugger would do it

definitions.text: That's not how the bugger would do it
definitions.note: a jokey description rather than a synonym

indicators.note: acting odd means behaving strangely, so the letters are put into a strange order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone behaves strangely over coffee, and the second sentence leers at sexual positions.
explanation.walkthrough: Sodomy is performed from behind, so the bugger would not be facing his partner.
explanation.definitionFit: Face to face means directly confronting each other, the opposite of approaching from behind.

clue.text: Lord Gnome's vital statistics even more dull before consuming the hard stuff

definitions.note: a noun phrase for the activity of working out figures

blocks.note: more numb means more dulled in feeling
hard food is crunched while it is eaten

explanation.surface: The proprietor's sales figures are getting duller, before he hits the spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord Gnome is Private Eye's fictional proprietor. 'The hard stuff' suggests strong drink, but it is crunchy food.
explanation.definitionFit: Number crunching is the processing of large amounts of figures, such as a proprietor's circulation statistics.

clue.text: Spiteful thing, Ann Widdecombe finally in the shit

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter only of the surname
in places the preceding pieces inside the word that follows

blocks.note: taken as written
the last letter of the surname
in the shit means in a mess

explanation.walkthrough: Ann Widdecombe is a former British Conservative minister.
explanation.definitionFit: Meanness is unkindness or spite, so a mean act is a spiteful one.

clue.text: Rather unsteady with an erection? Get a move on!

blocks.note: giddy means dizzy and unsteady
something erected is up

explanation.surface: A wobbly man with an erection is told to hurry up.
explanation.definitionFit: Giddy-up is the call to a horse urging it to go faster, so an order to hurry.

clue.text: Balls trailing after Ray screwed?

blocks.note: a shaft of light is a ray
Ed Balls is a Labour politician

explanation.surface: A rude question about whether someone called Ray had sex.
explanation.walkthrough: Balls looks like the word for testicles, but it is the surname of the politician Ed Balls.
explanation.definitionFit: Shafted is slang for cheated or badly treated, as is screwed.

clue.text: Met. in trouble (infiltrating Congress) – explosive stuff

indicators.note: something in trouble is in disarray, so its letters are disturbed
to infiltrate is to get inside, so one piece enters the other

congress is a formal word for sexual intercourse

explanation.surface: London's Metropolitan Police in a scandal infiltrating the US Congress, with explosive revelations.
explanation.walkthrough: The Met is London's Metropolitan Police; Congress looks like the US legislature but means sex.
explanation.definitionFit: Semtex is a plastic explosive made in Czechoslovakia, used in bombings.

clue.text: 'Tone' forced to pussyfoot being PC?

a cat's foot has soft pads

explanation.surface: Tony Blair, nicknamed Tone, is made to tread carefully to stay politically correct.
explanation.walkthrough: PC looks like political correctness, but it means a personal computer.

clue.text: Depp's movie activity, being self-righteous and vulgar

blocks.note: pi is slang for pious or sanctimonious
racy means risqué or slightly indecent

clue.text: City's major financial, etc. centre – Brown after bloke with cover

a hat is a head covering

clue.text: (& 25ac.) Tray misused as a windbreaker, Brian Sewell fashion?

clue.text: Sod all in tabloid uplifting, which makes good sense

the Roman numeral for one
